subject: health
title: Food Safety and Allergies
about: Washing hands and fruit, keeping cold food cold, tossing food that fell on the floor or smells bad, mold, what a food allergy is and the signs (itchy mouth, swollen lips) that mean get a grown-up fast, keeping your lunch to yourself, only eating what a grown-up says is safe, and hot ovens, hot soup and raw dough. NC 1.PCH.1.1 and 1.PCH.1.2 (germs cause illness and how to stop them) with 1.NPA.1.2 (foods and why we eat them) and 1.PCH.2.2 (burn hazards); builds on Germs and Handwashing.
tip: Let him be the fruit washer before snack and the lunchbox ice-pack checker before school.

cards.q: What do you do to an apple before you eat it?
cards.note: Rub it under running water, even if you plan to peel it.

cards.q: Why do we wash fruit before eating it?
cards.note: Fruit travels a long way from the farm. Lots of hands touch it before yours.

cards.q: You are helping make sandwiches. What do you wash first?
cards.note: Soap and water for 20 seconds before you touch any food.

cards.q: You pour a glass of milk. Where does the milk carton go next?
cards.note: Milk, meat, eggs and yogurt stay cold so germs cannot grow in them.

cards.q: What keeps the yogurt in your lunchbox cold until lunchtime?
cards.note: Cold food stays safe for a few hours with an ice pack. Pack it right next to the yogurt.

cards.q: Your cracker falls on the floor. What do you do with it?
wrong: put it back in the box
cards.note: Floors have germs even when they look clean. Get a fresh cracker.

cards.q: The milk smells sour and yucky. What do you do?
cards.note: A bad smell is your nose warning you. Food that smells off goes out.

cards.q: Bread has green fuzzy spots on it. What is that?
cards.note: Mold means the bread is too old to eat. Show a grown-up and toss it.

cards.q: Some kids get very sick if they eat peanuts. What is that called?
cards.note: Peanuts, milk, eggs and tree nuts are common allergies. Those kids stay safe by staying away from that food.

cards.q: After eating, a friend's lips swell and their mouth itches. What do you do?
cards.note: Swelling, itching, hives or trouble breathing after food means a grown-up is needed right away.

cards.q: Your friend has a milk allergy. Should you share your yogurt?
cards.note: Even a tiny bite can make a kid with an allergy very sick. Keep your lunch yours.

cards.q: Why does a school have a nut-free table?
cards.note: Kids with nut allergies sit where no nuts are near. It keeps lunch safe for everyone.

cards.q: You try a new food and your mouth feels itchy or tingly. What should you do?
cards.note: An itchy mouth or a tummy ache after a new food is worth telling about. A grown-up can check.

cards.q: You find berries growing on a bush outside. Do you eat them?
wrong: yes, if a bird eats them
cards.note: Some wild berries and mushrooms are poison. Only eat what a grown-up says is safe.

cards.q: A kid at the park offers you a snack from their bag. What is the safe thing to do?
cards.note: Your grown-up knows what is safe for you to eat.

cards.q: Cookies are baking in the oven. Who opens the oven door?
cards.note: The oven, the door and the pan are all very hot. Stay back until a grown-up says it has cooled.

cards.q: Your soup is steaming hot. What do you do?
cards.note: Steam means hot. Little sips from the edge of the spoon once it cools.

cards.q: The cookie dough has raw egg in it. When is it safe to eat?
cards.note: Raw egg and raw flour can carry germs. Baking kills them.
